issues.detail: Mostly covers happy-path setup and tests; lacks troubleshooting for common failures such as WebDriverAgent signing errors, emulator boot timeouts, stale element or session errors, and WebView context switching for hybrid apps.

scenarios.name: fix-invalid-capabilities-android-emulator
scenarios.rationale: Both add the `appium:` prefix correctly, keep platformName bare and use `appium:avd`, but B explicitly says deviceName doesn't select a device on Android and drops it, while A keeps a prefixed deviceName and only notes in a code comment that Android ignores it for selection.

scenarios.name: wdio-config-and-accessibility-id-test
scenarios.rationale: Both install the required packages and give UiAutomator2 capabilities with appium: keys, services: ['appium'], mocha, $('~...') selectors and waitForDisplayed; B wins because it installs appium locally so the service starts it with no extra step. A installs appium globally, uses ESM `export const config` in a .js file that may fail under CommonJS, and omits the spec reporter and local runner, while B uses CommonJS and adds service options, though B omits explicit webdriverio and @wdio/cli install of webdriverio (it installs @wdio/cli and @wdio/local-runner but not webdriverio itself).

scenarios.name: android-swipe-gesture-python
scenarios.rationale: Both use `execute_script` with `mobile: swipeGesture` and `mobile: longClickGesture` with the right parameters, but B explains the TouchAction removal, gives a coordinate alternative and a W3C Actions fallback, and mentions updating the uiautomator2 driver. A adds a good test structure but is thinner on the Appium 3 context. Neither shows `UiAutomator2Options` setup, and A also contains an odd reference to "the reference" that the user never supplied.
